text: CoinEx Founder: Binance Incident Exposed Three Entirely Avoidable Security and Operational Flaws Haipo Yang, Founder of CoinEx, stated that the recent Binance security breach exposed at least three critical mistakes that were entirely avoidable, underscoring a failure of operational discipline rather than a lack of sophisticated technology. First, development and operations environments lacked strict isolation; production access should be restricted to dedicated hardware free of third-party software, separating daily communication and browsing onto independent devices. Second, the operations stack lacked meaningful two-factor authentication (2FA), enabling full production compromise via a single leaked credential rather than enforcing hardware-bound MFA through tools like AWS Session Manager. Third, the MPC multi-signature setup existed in name only, as signers failed to conduct substantive independent verifications, causing the entire scheme to collapse upon a single node breach; Yang emphasized that multisig mechanisms are only effective when signers maintain mutual distrust and independently validate each raw transaction rather than blind-signing upstream requests. — link

text: Analyst: Suspected North Korean Hackers Moved $1.46M via Jupiter Lend and Circle Bridge; Jupiter Says Funds Remain Traceable On-chain analyst @FabianoSolana reported that suspected North Korean hackers moved approximately $1.46 million through Jupiter Lend and Circle's cross-chain bridge. Funds from an FBI-flagged Solana wallet (AffzFD) were routed through roughly 35 intermediary wallets, consolidated, and deposited into Jupiter Lend before a new wallet withdrew a similar amount minutes later. The funds were then swapped into USDC, bridged through Noble and dYdX, and returned to Solana. The analyst reported 16 outbound transfers totaling $1,463,410 and 19 inbound transfers totaling $1,463,400, with no funds frozen. Jupiter COO Kash Dhanda clarified that the attackers only deposited and withdrew funds through Jupiter Lend, unlike an earlier Aave incident involving borrowing non-freezable assets against stolen stablecoins. He said the funds remained fully traceable through LP tokens, with wallet associations preserved, and that Jupiter's security team monitored the activity in real time. As of publication, Circle had not publicly addressed the transfers or explained why the funds were not frozen. — link

text: Binance Details $6.34B Hack: Fake Job Interviews Used to Plant Malware, Internal AI Tool Exploited Binance released an initial report on its October 29 hack, revealing that attackers used fake job interviews and malware to compromise an engineer's device in September. They later exploited an internal AI tool to gain access to wallet engineers, then used stolen credentials to compromise a wallet signing service and abuse Ethereum's EIP-7702 authorization mechanism. Binance said withdrawal suspensions alone could not stop the malicious on-chain authorizations, which required a separate revocation process. Of the $6.34 billion in affected assets, approximately $2.85 billion has been frozen or intercepted. Binance said 98% of affected token assets had been replenished as of October 31, with sufficient funds set aside to cover all losses. The investigation remains ongoing. — link
